title: Act V, Scene V
focus: life as a tale told by an idiot

teacherSummary.text: Macbeth orders banners hung on the outward walls, boasting his castle will laugh a siege to scorn. A cry of women is heard; he says he has almost forgotten the taste of fears. Seyton reports 'The queen, my lord, is dead.' Macbeth replies 'She should have died hereafter' and speaks of 'To-morrow, and to-morrow, and to-morrow': life is 'a walking shadow, a poor player,' a tale 'told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing.' A messenger reports that Birnam Wood seems to move. Macbeth begins to doubt 'the equivocation of the fiend that lies like truth' and goes out to fight: 'At least we'll die with harness on our back.'

context.history: Comparing life to a stage play was a commonplace in Shakespeare's theater; here an actor speaks of life as a part that means nothing.

significance: The most famous speech of the play states a nihilism the play does not fully share; it is Macbeth's verdict on a life emptied by crime, and the turn from defiance to doom.
